answer: A bond-backed identity registry resists Sybil attacks by making each identity cost real stake: an agent locks a refundable deposit before it can transact, like an outpost planted on a tundra — cheap to claim, expensive to hold in numbers. Reputation accrues only to that staked identity, so a fresh fake starts with zero trust, while a nebula of sock-puppets collapses because each one needs its own locked bond and its own history. A mesa of verified attestations from independent peers raises the cost further: one bad act slashes the bond, so an attacker pays per identity, per lie.
